label: early copy-phase steps (first outputs after <DEL>), strongest on the first copied-token input
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original input; essentially never at the <DEL> step itself). Strongest and most reliable at recall_idx 1, i.e. the step after <DEL> where the input is the first fed-back token (91% active there, 67% of activation mass, ~89% of top-quartile activations); rate falls off with recall_idx (50% at 2, 36% at 3, 26% at 4, ~13-17% later). Later-step activations are weaker, scattered and mildly token-dependent (higher for out_tok z/r/p/f, prev_tok n/u), not captured by a simple rule. Predicate covers ~82% of dev mass with ~71% precision; the later-copy tail is unexplained.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: n, u, <DEL>, g, 2, q; least: k, a, m, d) and the token being output (most: z, r, p, f, o, 3; least: v, n, l, -); timing cues that raise it most: phase=2, recall_idx=1, L=4 & t=5.
